solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Actor's timeless performance in first working role?

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened performance goes inside the job

parts.note: a job is a working role

indicators.note: timeless asks for the time abbreviation T to be dropped from the word for a performance

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
T is the standard abbreviation for time
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: An actor's breakout turn in the first job he landed, played without any sense of time.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the Roman numeral one, so 'first'; Derek Jacobi has appeared in Christie adaptations, a nod to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Derek Jacobi is a celebrated English stage and screen performer, known for I, Claudius.

clue.text: In a passage this rich, a suspect is introduced — my characters all around

indicators.note: is introduced says the jumbled letters are brought into the middle of a gate

parts.note: a gate is a passage through a wall or fence

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, taken just as written

explanation.surface: A detective-story moment: in a rich man's passageway, a suspect is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the setter speaking as the author: her characters fill the whole grid, so 'my characters all around' identifies their creator.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle's other themed entries are all creations of this crime novelist, so they are 'my characters' from her point of view.

clue.text: See 20 down
Character Tuppence supports rumbling joint capers

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
rumbling suggests a jolting, disturbed motion, so the letters of joint capers are thrown about

parts.note: tuppence is two pence, written as two Ps

explanation.surface: Someone called Tuppence is propping up a gang whose schemes have been found out at the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuppence is also a Christie heroine (of Tommy and Tuppence), which sharpens the theme; here she just means two pence, PP, placed under the anagram of JOINT CAPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Japp is the Scotland Yard policeman who often works alongside Poirot in the novels.

clue.text: Hotel croupier — dodgy character

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are shaken out of order

explanation.surface: A casino croupier at a hotel is a shady figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is the Belgian sleuth who is the most famous figure in her fiction.

clue.text: Before taking me off home, caught one's first fish

indicators.note: Before says the first two pieces come ahead of the shortened home

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of one
taking ... off together say the letters of me are removed
taking ... off together say the letters of me are removed from home

explanation.surface: Before setting off home, an angler has caught his first fish of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's first' is the first letter of 'one'; C is the scorecard abbreviation in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a species of Pacific salmon, also called silver salmon.

clue.text: Picking up something criminal left behind? That will do detective

indicators.note: picking up means catching a sound, so the pieces are read by how they are spoken

parts.words: something criminal left behind? That will do
parts.note: a clue is evidence a criminal leaves behind, and so means that will do; said together they give the French name

explanation.surface: A detective picks up evidence left at a crime scene and declares the job done.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, CLUE SO sounds like the French name, 'kloo-zo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Clouseau is the bungling French policeman of the Pink Panther films.

clue.text: See 19
When we're getting lots of cards but missing a letter?

definitions.text: When we're getting lots of cards

parts.note: something missing is not there: no
EL is the spelt-out name of the letter L

explanation.surface: A time when cards pour in, but one letter has gone astray in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is how the letter L is written out in words; read the answer as 'no L' and the second half makes sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a name for Christmas, the festival when greetings cards arrive by the dozen.

clue.text: Transmits vocally so long after writing?

indicators.note: after says the farewell follows the R

parts.note: writing is one of the three Rs of basic education, so R
adios is Spanish for goodbye, as is so long

explanation.surface: Someone speaks a farewell aloud after having first written it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so any of them can give R.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio a message is to broadcast it by voice over the airwaves, a verb in the third person here.

clue.text: Ostentatious look for university in particular

indicators.note: look for university means put the word for look in place of U

parts.note: particular in the sense of choosy means fussy
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A showy appearance stands in for academic distinction, in one case.
explanation.definitionFit: Flossy is informal for showy or flashy, overly decorated in style.

clue.text: Character blessing something worthless

parts.note: felicity is great happiness, a blessing
a lemon is a dud, something useless

explanation.surface: A blessing that turns out to be a useless thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Felicity Lemon is Poirot's efficient secretary in the Christie stories.

clue.text: Planner's shading the fourth Teletubby red

parts.note: the Teletubbies are Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po, the fourth
Che Guevara was a famous red, a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A designer colours in the smallest Teletubby in red.
explanation.walkthrough: The Teletubbies are characters from a British pre-school TV show; Po is the small red one, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Poché is the architectural term for solid areas filled in or hatched on a building plan.

clue.text: Broadcast uses bog standard joke

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: bog is British slang for toilet, and to use it is to wee

explanation.surface: A broadcast relies on a tired, ordinary gag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog standard' looks like the British phrase for mediocre, but bog goes with uses and standard with joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is British slang for a trick or a stock gag that gets repeated.

clue.text: Quean is more stylish nude

indicators.note: nude means stripped, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: classier means more stylish

explanation.surface: A queen is apparently more elegant without her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Quean is not a misspelt queen: it is a Scots word for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage a quean is a girl or young woman, much like a lassie.

clue.text: 'Welcome to Honolulu' written in invisible ink

indicators.note: written in says the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A greeting to Hawaii has been penned in secret ink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is the garland of flowers placed round a visitor's neck as a Hawaiian greeting.

clue.text: Regulars going off to seek price list

indicators.note: regulars are letters at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: Regular customers leave to go looking for a price list.
explanation.walkthrough: The FTSE 100 is the London Stock Exchange index, apt in the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE index is a published table of share prices on the London exchange.

clue.text: Do like retro rap

parts.note: to char is to clean, to do the housework for someone

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: e.g. means for example, so like

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform in old-school rap style.
explanation.walkthrough: Do looks like a verb of imitation; it means clean, as a charwoman does.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is slang for a criminal charge, as in taking the rap.

clue.text: I'm annoyed our fancy hotel's introduced a song and dance

indicators.note: introduced says the reworked letters and H are put into the exclamation

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of irritation

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or embellish, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated that a posh hotel has started putting on a cabaret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the hotel, but it rearranges our; H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is a fuss or commotion, just what a brouhaha is.

clue.text: See 2
Not having taken the odds, last hurrah bizarrely pains character

indicators.note: bizarrely means oddly, so the letters are jumbled
dropping the odd letters keeps only the even ones of last

parts.note: stings are sharp pains

explanation.surface: A gambler who did not take the odds finds a final celebration painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last hurrah' looks like one phrase, but only 'last' is thinned to its even letters before joining hurrah in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Arthur Hastings is Poirot's friend and narrator, his Watson figure.

clue.text: Pretentious sleuth's enemy has bumped researchers off

indicators.note: has bumped ... off together mean killed, so the researchers are removed
has bumped ... off together mean killed, so the researchers are removed

parts.note: Professor Moriarty is Sherlock Holmes's arch-enemy
MORI is a British opinion-polling and market research firm

explanation.surface: Holmes's nemesis has murdered some scientists, as a pretentious villain would.
explanation.walkthrough: MORI is the pollster now called Ipsos MORI; take it from MORIARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone affecting artistic taste in a showy, pretentious way.

clue.text: Character's song finishing up musical

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: finishing means the end
Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: A character's big number brings a musical to its close.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne Oliver is the crime novelist who helps Poirot, a self-portrait of her creator.

clue.text: Trojan styles not this grating

indicators.note: styles as a verb means fashions or shapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Trojan's fashion sense is apparently not this annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TROJAN are those of the answer plus N, O, T, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a harsh, discordant vibration or sound, a grating.

clue.text: See 5
The first of the French hands has changed bulb

indicators.note: the first of the two Ls is the one to change
L and R are left and right hands, so swapping hands turns L to R

parts.note: Gallic means French

explanation.surface: The leading French hand has altered how it grips the bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: GALLIC has two Ls; change the first from L (left) to R (right) and the other hand appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of this pungent plant is a bulb made up of cloves.

clue.text: Baltic port awarded gold stars

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Riga is the Latvian capital and port on the Baltic

explanation.surface: A Baltic city has been given a gold medal for excellence.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriga, the Charioteer, is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Sponge I see on sweet counter

indicators.note: on in an across entry means the exclamation follows
counter means running against, so the dessert is reversed

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit dessert, a sweet
ah is said when understanding: I see

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sponge cake on the counter of a sweet shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Sponge and sweet pull towards cake; the definition is the bath sponge, and a fool is a fruit dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd fibre used as a scrubbing bath sponge.

clue.text: The rest a bit outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: The remainder of a statement is a little too blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace means quiet repose, rest from noise and activity.

clue.text: PC ready in dock

indicators.note: in places the word for ready inside the word for dock

parts.note: to dock a tail is to lop it
apt means ready or inclined

explanation.surface: A personal computer is set up and waiting in its docking station.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock looks like a computer docking station; it means cut, LOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer.

clue.text: See 30
Cleverly works this dope

parts.note: James Cleverly, Foreign Secretary in 2023, works in the Foreign Office; dope is slang for inside knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone shrewdly turns a fool to his advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleverly is a person: James Cleverly was the British Foreign Secretary in 2023, so his workplace is IN FO, the Foreign Office. Dope is the definition, information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, the lowdown or gen.

clue.text: Character name changed in beer games, litre drunk

indicators.note: in places the rearranged name inside the jar

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of name are rearranged
drunk means swallowed, so the games take in the litre

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games

explanation.surface: A name gets mangled during drinking games after a litre has been downed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a jar is a pint of beer, and PE (physical education) is school games.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Jane Marple is the elderly village sleuth of St Mary Mead in the Christie novels.

clue.text: Steam or water, then preparation time

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically as two words: steam and liquid water are H2O in any state but the frozen one
second meaning: advance warning that leaves time to get ready

explanation.surface: A recipe step: get your steam or water going, then allow time to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: Steam or water describes H2O in any state but frozen: NOT ICE, which run together is the word for time given to get ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Notice is advance warning, the period given to prepare before something happens.
